{{Short description|Canadian mathematician}}
[[File:Bruce Reed, Bellairs 2015.jpg|thumb|240px|Bruce Reed at the [[Bellairs Research Institute]], 2015]]
'''Bruce Alan Reed''' <small>[[Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]]</small> is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]], a former [[Canada Research Chair]] in Graph Theory at [[McGill University]].<ref name="mcgill">{{citation |url=https://www.cs.mcgill.ca/people/faculty/|title=McGill School of Computer Science|website=McGill.ca|access-date=28 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="crc"/> His research is primarily in [[graph theory]].<ref name="crc">[http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileID=102 Chairholders: Bruce A. Reed], Canada Research Chairs, retrieved 2012-10-07.</ref> He is a distinguished research fellow of the Institute of Mathematics in the [[Academia Sinica]], Taiwan,<ref name="sinica">{{citation|url=https://www.math.sinica.edu.tw/www/people/websty1_20e.jsp?owner=brucealanreed|title=Bruce Alan Reed|work=Research and specialist staff|publisher=Institute of Mathematics, Academia Sinica|access-date=2023-11-07}}</ref> and an adjunct professor at the [[University of Victoria]] in Canada.<ref name="uvic">{{citation|url=https://www.uvic.ca/science/math-statistics/research/home/discrete-math/index.php|title=Discrete mathematics|work=Mathematics & Statistics|publisher=University of Victoria|access-date=2023-11-07}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Reed earned his Ph.D. in 1986 from McGill, under the supervision of [[Vašek Chvátal]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=101779}}</ref> Before returning to McGill as a Canada Research Chair, Reed held positions at the [[University of Waterloo]], [[Carnegie Mellon University]], and the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]].<ref>[http://www.pims.math.ca/pims-glance/scientific-review-panel/past-members Past members], Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences, retrieved 2012-10-07.</ref>

Reed was elected as a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2009,<ref>{{citation|url=http://publications.mcgill.ca/reporter/2009/10/three-mcgill-researchers-to-be-inducted-as-rsc-fellows/|title=Three McGill researchers elected RSC Fellows|journal=McGill Reporter|date=October 1, 2009|access-date=October 7, 2012|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303171908/http://publications.mcgill.ca/reporter/2009/10/three-mcgill-researchers-to-be-inducted-as-rsc-fellows/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and is the recipient of the 2013 [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize|CRM-Fields-PIMS Prize]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.pims.math.ca/news/bruce-reed-announced-2013-crmfieldspims-prize-recipient/|title=Bruce Reed announced as 2013 CRM/Fields/PIMS Prize recipient|access-date=2012-12-30|archive-date=2015-04-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150418002327/http://www.pims.math.ca/news/bruce-reed-announced-2013-crmfieldspims-prize-recipient|url-status=dead}}, Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences, retrieved 2012-12-30.</ref>

In 2021 he left McGill, and subsequently became a researcher at the Academia Sinica and an adjunct professor at the University of Victoria.<ref name="mcgill"/><ref name="sinica"/><ref name="uvic"/>

==Research==
Reed's thesis research concerned [[perfect graph]]s.<ref name="mg"/>
With Michael Molloy, he is the author of a book on [[graph coloring]] and the [[probabilistic method]].<ref>Kayll, P. Mark (2003). Graph Colouring and the Probabilistic Method. ''Mathematical Reviews'', {{MR|1869439}}.</ref> Reed has also published highly cited papers on the [[giant component]] in [[random graph]]s with a given [[degree sequence]],{{ran|MR95}}{{ran|MR98a}} random [[satisfiability problem]]s,{{ran|CR92}} [[acyclic coloring]],{{ran|AMR91}} [[tree decomposition]],{{ran|R92}}{{ran|R97}} and constructive versions of the [[Lovász local lemma]].{{ran|MR98b}}

He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2002.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=2015-10-01|archive-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> His talk there concerned a proof by Reed and [[Benny Sudakov]], using the [[probabilistic method]], of a conjecture by Kyoji Ohba that graphs whose number of vertices and [[chromatic number]] are (asymptotically) within a factor of two of each other have equal chromatic number and [[list coloring|list chromatic number]].{{ran|RS02}}
